cards.explanation: The answer is Sit at My right hand, friends. The LORD says to David's Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” (Psalm 110:1) Notice He says sit. The footstool is the part the LORD says He will make.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” (Psalm 110:1) Look at who is doing the work there, friends. The LORD says “I make.” So David's Lord gets to sit while the LORD takes care of it.

The answer is Rule in the midst of Your enemies. The LORD extends the scepter from Zion and says, “Rule in the midst of Your enemies.” (Psalm 110:2) A scepter is what a ruler holds, so the words fit it. And the rule happens right in the middle of those enemies, which is a bold place to set up shop.

The answer is False, friends, and that's the whole point of the line. David says, “Your people shall be willing on Your day of battle.” (Psalm 110:3) Willing is the word he uses. Though I will say a plate of cookies never hurt anybody's attendance.

The answer is False. The psalm says, “The LORD has sworn and will not change His mind…” (Psalm 110:4). I once promised myself I'd only eat one broken cookie per batch. The LORD's oath is a different kind of promise, friends, because He will not change His mind.

The answer is priest. The LORD swears, “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.” (Psalm 110:4) The verse says the LORD has sworn and will not change His mind. That oath is what the word forever stands on, friends.

The answer is kings, friends. David says, “The Lord is at Your right hand; He will crush kings in the day of His wrath.” (Psalm 110:5) It's a heavy verse, and I think it's okay to let it be heavy. The word to hold on to is kings.

The answer is True. David says of Him, “He will judge the nations, heaping up the dead…” (Psalm 110:6). Look back at verse 5 and you'll see it's about the same One who crushes kings. That One also judges the nations, friends.

The answer is Lift up His head. That's how the psalm ends: “He will drink from the brook by the road; therefore He will lift up His head.” (Psalm 110:7) See that word therefore? The head lifting comes because of the drink. That's a quiet ending after a loud psalm, friends.
